svg.title: TA419 AI-policy phishing kill chain - reply-first lure, fake OneDrive, Frameless BitB AitM and Microsoft session capture
svg.desc: Two-lane kill chain. Left lane, the targeted AI policy expert and their Microsoft 365 account: 1 a benign first-contact email from an impersonated expert with no link, 2 the reply-first gate after which a shortened URL arrives, 3 the redirect chain through a first-stage domain with a Cloudflare Turnstile check and a fake OneDrive loading screen, 4 the Frameless BitB fake browser window over a fake OneDrive page, 5 the adversary-in-the-middle relay to the real Microsoft sign-in where MFA passes, 6 capture of the session cookie while the victim sees a normal sign-in, 7 session replay and follow-on activity, which Proofpoint does not describe. Right lane: A personas and sender addresses, B sending infrastructure, C the redirect domain list, D the BitB script paths, E the telemetry and OTP automation module, F attribution and defence. Critical stages are shown in red. Detection anchors are the sender addresses and domains, the three script paths, the shared TLS certificate subject and the same Entra session ID used from a second IP.
svg.text: TA419 AI-policy phishing: Frameless BitB AitM on Microsoft sign-in
Vendor: Proofpoint - Date: 2026-10-05 - Cluster: TA419 (China-aligned, espionage) - Day 116
TARGET: AI POLICY EXPERT AND MICROSOFT 365 ACCOUNT
OPERATOR, INFRASTRUCTURE AND RESPONSE (published)
First contact: benign mail from a spoofed expert
Invitation to an AI Policy Advisory Committee or a Senate report
Persona: Lynne Edwards Parker, Heidi Crebo-Rediker, Anthropic staff
No link and no attachment, so filters have nothing to score
iocs.csv: 3 sender addresses, 4 lookalike domains
Reply-first gate: target replies, short URL follows
The link is sent only after the recipient replies
Mail from VPS hosts; some via residential proxies
Shared self-signed TLS certificate on a high port
cert SHA-256 b314a149...744460 (O=Castro Inc)
Redirect chain: first-stage domain and Turnstile
Shortened URL then a first-stage domain behind Cloudflare
Turnstile check filters scanners; fake OneDrive loading screen
Second-stage domain hosts the AitM page
driftshare[.]co -> globalfileshareplatform[.]com
Frameless BitB: fake browser on fake OneDrive
Shadow DOM fake OneDrive folder; attacker OneDrive via 1drv.ms
Permission-denied banner triggers a fake Chrome sign-in window
Built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript only, no iframe
/secondary/script.js /primary/script.js
AitM relay to the real Microsoft sign-in, MFA passes
Real /common/oauth2/v2.0/authorize response with injected scripts
OfficeHome client_id 4765445b-32c6-49b0-83e6-1d93765276ca
Password, MFA and conditional-access checks pass to Microsoft
/secondary/observe.js tracks progress, sends OTPs
Session cookie captured; victim sees normal sign-in
Cookie captured by the proxy after the relayed sign-in
Keep me signed in is accepted automatically
Victim lands in a normal signed-in state (The Hacker News)
Entra: interactive sign-in with MFA from the victim IP
Session replay and follow-on: not described
A stolen session works until revoked; password reset is not enough
No mailbox access, data theft or persistence is reported
No source states that any account was compromised
Hunt: same SessionId from a second IP and ASN
A
Personas, pretexts and sender addresses
leparker@mail[.]com, hcrediker@mail[.]com, hcrediker@outlook[.]com
Lookalikes: tw-koryu[.]org, heritiages[.]org, heritiage[.]org,
shinjirou[.]info (Japan-Taiwan Assoc., Heritage, Koizumi)
Feb 2026 subject: Military Integration of Claude feedback
first seen Feb to Jul 2026
Proofpoint 2026-10-01
B
Sending infrastructure: VPS and residential proxies
First-hop Received header showed VPS 108.61.163[.]187
Self-signed certificate shared across sending servers
Subject C=US, ST=Kansas, L=Millsstad, O=Castro Inc, CN=CI
Single IP observation: verify before any block
cert first seen February 2026
Zeek x509 and Suricata tls.cert_subject
C
Redirect domains: 8 first-stage, 7 second-stage
First-stage: driftshare, quickfly, cirrushare, goshshare,
synchvault, msfile, winsync, sharehub
Second-stage: globalfileshareplatform, smartsyncbox, ...
Typically NameSilo registrar; Cloudflare hides origin
first seen Dec 2025 to Jul 2026
pairing by month is inference, not stated
D
Kit: modified open-source Frameless BitB
Base by Wael Masri (January 2024), Evilginx phishlet,
server-side substitution rules for Microsoft 365
primary/script.js hooks clicks and touch events and
watches for the OneDrive permission-denied banner
YARA TA419_BitB_Phishing_Page_Kit_Markers
Sigma 03 proxy paths
E
Telemetry and automation module
observe.js reports the sign-in position to the operator
Live session view; auto-accepts Keep me signed in
Auto-submits one-time codes once validated
Suggests operators expect code or push MFA factors
Suricata sid 6330005 /secondary/observe.js
KQL k3 replay by SessionId
F
Attribution, scope and defence
TA419: China-aligned, espionage-motivated; since April 2025
Likely supports Chinese intelligence aims (Proofpoint)
UNK_SweetSpecter is a separate cluster; no CVE involved
Passkeys, origin-bound MFA; verify outreach out of band
Proofpoint: likely; no confidence level or agency given
no CVE is used by this campaign
Detection anchors: sender addresses and lookalike domains, kit script paths, shared TLS certificate subject, same SessionId from a second IP
Rules in this folder: Sigma 01-04, KQL k1-k4, YARA ta419_bitb_phishing_page_and_lure.yar (2 rules), Suricata sids 6330001-6330006, PEAK hunts H1-H3.
Indicators are dated Dec 2025 to Jul 2026; Proofpoint gives no takedown status. The first email has no link, so the sender is the earliest signal.
A password reset does not end a stolen session: revoke sessions, review MFA methods and mailbox rules, and move targets to phishing-resistant sign-in.
